inputs.source: Vendor quote emails and attachments from external senders

instructions.note: Manager approval covers item and budget before any quote exists. The orchestrator then autonomously selects the vendor and bank details and delegates payment, but the design treats that earlier approval as if it authorized the specific payment (TC7 authority laundering).

The prompt asserts 'Payments-agent will handle any remaining checks,' but runtime notes state payments-agent trusts any task from the bearer token and pays the bank details supplied with no further verification. The stated safety assumption is false.
No limit is stated on purchase amount, quote count, or payment frequency the orchestrator may delegate.

controls.name: Manager approval of purchase request (item and budget)
controls.decay_rationale: A human approval gate is capability independent, but it authorizes only item and budget before any vendor or bank detail exists, so it provides no protection over the later payment delegation step.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: pay only vendors on the approved list
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model to match the vendor name against the approved list and resist a fraudulent quote. It does not validate bank account details, so a sender using an approved vendor's name with substituted bank details still passes. A more capable or manipulated model more readily rationalizes a plausible match.

controls.name: Recipient/destination confirmation bound to system-of-record vendor bank details
controls.decay_rationale: Destination verified against a record the model cannot edit would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Approval context propagation and scope validation at payments-agent
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by payments-agent validating a signed approval record rather than trusting the orchestrator's bearer token alone.

controls.name: Raw-action human approval gate on fund release
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action, low-volume approval gate at the point of payment release does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Pin/sign payments-agent card and verify peer identity
controls.decay_rationale: Pinned, signed definitions and verified peer identity (mTLS or signed identity) close the rug-pull and impersonation path regardless of model capability.

controls.name: Rate and spend cap on payment delegation
controls.decay_rationale: A hard cap enforced outside the model bounds cumulative exposure regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit trail linking approval to payment
controls.decay_rationale: A provenance record the model cannot forge makes later attribution possible regardless of model behavior.

findings.title: Business email compromise pattern: untrusted vendor quote determines payment destination (TC1 variant)

attack_path.note: Unauthenticated external email supplies a 'quote' including bank details.
Orchestrator uses 'the bank details from the chosen quote' and delegates payment.
Pays the bank details in the task with no further verification.

forecast.watch_signal: Model or version upgrade for the orchestrator, or evidence of longer unattended task horizons, without an added destination-verification control.

evidence.observation: Vendor quotes arrive by email from outside the company.
Agent is told to 'choose the best one' and 'Use the bank details from the chosen quote,' taking bank details directly from untrusted email content.
'Only pay vendors on the approved list' checks vendor identity by name only; nothing checks that bank details in the quote match the approved vendor's known account.

recommendations.action: Verify payment destination (bank account/routing) against a system-of-record for the approved vendor before releasing payment; hold or reject if the quote's bank details do not match known-good records.
Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate for first-time or changed vendor bank details before cap.delegate_payment executes.
Verify sender authenticity of vendor quote emails (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) and require out-of-band confirmation for new or changed bank details.

findings.title: Authority laundering and confused deputy: item/budget approval treated as authorization for an arbitrary payment (TC7)

threat_refs.name: Autonomous AI Agent Communication: Direct Agent Communication

forecast.watch_signal: A new payments-capable peer is added, or the orchestrator/payments-agent pairing is granted more autonomy, without adding approval-context propagation or peer identity verification.

evidence.observation: The manager approves the purchase request (item and budget) before any quote exists. The approval record is not passed to payments-agent.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token and pays the bank details in the task.
Authentication is a bare bearer token scheme with no mention of per-task scoping or signed approval context.
The agent card is fetched at startup and is not signed or pinned.

recommendations.action: Propagate the human approval's scope (item, budget, and once chosen, the specific vendor and bank account) to payments-agent, and require payments-agent to validate the task against that scope before paying.
Replace bearer-token-only trust with mutually authenticated, signed identity (mTLS or a signed, task-bound token), and pin/sign the payments-agent card so it cannot be silently redefined.
Add a raw-action, low-volume human approval gate immediately before fund release, independent of the orchestrator's bearer token.
Maintain a tamper-evident audit log linking the manager's approval record to the specific payment executed.

findings.title: No spend, rate, or step limit on payment delegation

forecast.watch_signal: Growth in purchase request volume or unattended task duration without an added spend/rate cap on payment delegation.

evidence.observation: No statement anywhere in the prompt of a maximum payment amount, payment count, or rate limit for cap.delegate_payment.
No runtime_config or IaC artifact was provided describing step, spend, or rate limits for the orchestrator or payments-agent.

recommendations.action: Impose a per-day/per-period spend cap and maximum payment count on cap.delegate_payment, enforced outside the model (for example in payments-agent or a payment gateway).
Alert on anomalous payment volume or velocity compared to historical baseline.

stride_coverage.rationale: Bearer-token-only auth to payments-agent means anyone holding or replaying the token can act as the orchestrator; no mTLS or signed identity is described.
No capability grants write or configure access to the orchestrator's own prompt, tools, or memory; nothing in the artifacts allows self-modification.
No attributable record ties the manager's item/budget approval to the specific vendor and bank details later chosen and paid.
No outbound disclosure channel beyond the payment delegation is described, which is assessed separately at flow.delegate_payment_a2a.
No step, rate, or spend limit is declared for purchase processing or payment delegation.
The orchestrator's delegated bearer-token authority lets it direct payments-agent to pay any vendor or amount, exceeding the manager's actual approval of only item and budget.
The agent card is fetched at startup, not signed or pinned, and peer identity is unverified; a spoofed or rug-pulled card could redirect the orchestrator's calls.
definitions_pinned is false, so payments-agent's declared skill or schema can change silently after the orchestrator's prompt was written (rug-pull vector).

payments-agent pays the bank details in the task with no mention of recording or verifying the human approval basis, so a fraudulent or out-of-scope payment cannot be traced back to an authorizing decision.
No further consumer of payments-agent's output is described beyond executing the payment; no additional disclosure path is evidenced.
No cap on the number or value of payments payments-agent will execute per orchestrator call.
payments-agent trusts any task from the orchestrator's bearer token with no check against the manager's approved scope, a textbook confused deputy.
Nothing verifies the vendor quote email's claimed sender identity against the approved vendor list before its bank details are used.
No attribution mechanism (signed email, verified sender) ties a quote's bank details to a real, approved vendor.
The design defines only a read capability (cap.vendor_list_read) on this store; no capability or input can write to it.
The list is read only for internal name-matching; no capability or input path sends its contents externally.
A single read per purchase request presents no meaningful resource-exhaustion surface; no loop or high-volume use of this read is described.
The external email is unauthenticated and its content (claimed vendor, bank details) can be freely set by the sender.
This is an inbound-only flow; it carries no organizational data outward.
Artifacts do not describe any volume or rate control on inbound vendor email processing, so denial-of-service risk at this edge cannot be assessed from what is given.
The payment task payload carries bank details sourced from an unauthenticated external quote, with no destination-account verification against a system of record.
Because payments-agent's identity is unverified and unpinned, the bearer token and payment payload sent over this flow could reach an impersonating endpoint.
No rate or spend cap bounds how many payment delegations this flow can carry.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an unauthenticated external vendor quote can directly determine the bank account paid via an irreversible, broad-credential payment delegation (untrusted source to severe sink). Residual stays high: the only control on that path is a behavioral vendor-name check that does not verify bank details and decays under model upgrade; no structural control binds the payment destination to a system of record, and the manager's approval authorizes item and budget only, before the sensitive step exists, so it earns no credit on cap.delegate_payment. A second, independent property finding shows the delegation to payments-agent does not propagate approval scope and the peer accepts any bearer-token request, enabling authority laundering and a confused deputy. A third shows no spend, rate, or step limit bounds cumulative exposure. Forecast returns to critical because a model upgrade (or longer task horizon) would defeat the sole credited control on the primary exfiltration-style payment path, and the other two findings hold at high with no controls currently credited to lose.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (system prompt, agent card, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual production behavior may differ.

No IaC, IAM policy, or payments-agent source/configuration was provided; payments-agent's actual credential scope and any internal checks are inferred from the runtime note that it 'trusts any task... and pays the bank details in the task,' which may understate or overstate real controls.

Approval volume for ctl.manager_approval is not stated, so its approval_volume is scored as unknown, which limits the credit it could otherwise receive and lowers confidence in the exact residual floor.
No details on email authentication (SPF/DKIM/DMARC) or vendor quote intake tooling were provided; the assessment assumes no such verification exists based on silence in the artifacts.
